items.title: Carry instructions, memory and notes into Do runs and automations
items.summary: Resolve the ADR-0003 chain (platform, org, Space, user persona, summoned agent) in one shared function used by both invoke_stream_sse (Ask) and agentic_run_stream (Do), and pass the result to execution-core through new RunAgentRequest fields so the loop's first system message carries it. At run start also reuse fetch_chat_memory_context (trivial-prompt gate, 400 ms bound, memory_recall provenance event) and recent thread turns, and give scheduled runs small per-task notes written with a version check; unattended runs read user memory but write only their own notes.
items.whyItMatters: A user who sets 'answer in Norwegian, I am a CFO' or whose preferences are already saved as memories, then launches an agent or a scheduled run, gets an agent that knows none of it. That is the most visible personalisation failure in the product and it directly undercuts the 'learns and tailors itself to its user' goal on the agent pages.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Layered instructions: 8 of 12 sources (table-stakes). Memory in agent tasks: 3 of 12 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude resolves seven instruction scopes with documented org > user precedence and per-scope character budgets in one assembler used by chat and agents; folder instructions are edited by the assistant as it learns. Cursor gives each automation a small versioned set of memory files that is listed and injected at run start and updated with compare-and-swap (expected_version), plus shared and per-conversation notes folders. Hermes adds the safety rule that unattended cron runs read memory but never write learned state.

items.approach: Model Plane only, in four steps. (1) Extract the ADR-0003 resolver from sse.rs into a shared module with the same per-layer budgets and precedence (org above persona), unit-tested for parity between both paths. (2) Add authored_instructions and memory_context string fields to RunAgentRequest (execution.proto; buf generate, mp-orchestration shim, parity tests) and have execution-core seed them into the first system message beside compose_system_prompt; show both in the run inspector. (3) In agentic_run_stream call fetch_chat_memory_context under the same trivial-prompt gate and emit the same memory_recall provenance event; include the last N thread turns. (4) Add a session-core run_notes table keyed by (org, user, task id) with a version column and a capability exposing list/get/update with expected_version; scheduled and unattended runs may read user memory but write only notes. Decide that subagents inherit the platform and org layers (authority) but not persona or memory.

items.title: Full-text search over past conversations, a recall tool and @thread references
items.summary: Phase 1: add a Postgres full-text index over thread messages in session-core, a SearchThreads RPC, a gateway chat-search route, a sidebar search box with highlighted snippets, and a recall_conversations agent tool (discover, scroll around a message, read) that makes no model call. Phase 2: let the composer @-mention a past thread and inject a bounded, immutable snapshot flagged as untrusted data, visible in the context inspector.
items.whyItMatters: Every comparable chat product has history search, and Verevon's sidebar can only substring-match titles it has already loaded. Search is also the cheapest recall mechanism for agents (zero model cost) and gives continuity across chats without growing memory; an @reference is transparent because the user picks what is carried over.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Search: 3 of 12 in the records (common, but table-stakes in practice since every chat product has it). Past-chat reference: 4 of 12 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes: one tool with four shapes (discover, scroll around an anchor, read, browse) and no LLM calls; BM25 ranked with recency decay, deduplicated by thread lineage, best hit hydrated in full and the rest returned as anchors with stable links, time bounds, cron sessions demoted; compaction archives rows (active=0) instead of deleting so they stay searchable. Cursor adds a user-facing FTS5 index with recency-weighted BM25 and highlighted snippets. DeepSeek: @label injects an immutable, bounded snapshot explicitly flagged untrusted, ranked by workspace affinity; Antigravity caps each field of a history summary by config.

items.title: Prove the skill-learning loop on real runs, with an eval and cost controls
items.summary: The loop RUN_COMPLETED -> sessionreview -> UpsertAgentSkill is wired and on by default, and the producer already withholds ZDR and waived runs. Build a seeded end-to-end check in which a real Do run authors a skill that a later turn matches and uses, run it as an automated eval, then settle which turns are reviewed (add an Ask-turn cadence if they are not) and put per-route model and spend controls on the reviewer.
items.whyItMatters: This loop is the product's answer to 'learns and tailors itself to its user'. Unproven it is a claim that already spends review money and sends transcripts to a separate model route; proven it is the main differentiator against ChatGPT and Claude, neither of which learns skills from work.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes forks a background review after the reply is delivered: only if a final response exists and the turn was not interrupted or unattended, it reviews a snapshot of the messages on a cheap model with whitelisted tools (memory, skill_manage) and read-before-write, capped at 16 iterations, with three prompt variants. Cadence counters trigger it (memory every 10 user turns; skills after 10 tool iterations without a skill write) and reset when the model already wrote. Corrections are routed into task-scoped skill rules. Its weakness is that it has no outcome evaluation, which Verevon's dissatisfaction quarantine already covers.

items.title: Stage learned skills as proposals with user and org approval
items.summary: Make every skill the background review writes start as a proposal, owned by the user whose run produced it and not matchable by anyone else, with a Settings > Learning inbox that shows the diff, the reason and a link to the source run. Accepting activates it for that user; promotion to org scope needs an org admin decision signed by Control. Unattended writers may only add, never replace or remove.
items.whyItMatters: UpsertAgentSkillRequest carries only an org_id, so a skill distilled from one user's private conversation becomes matchable for the whole org with no review. That is an authority and privacy problem, not only a UX one, and it blocks safe rollout of the learning loop. An inbox also makes learning visible, which is what sells it.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Manus records each learning proposal as a KnowledgeEvent {CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE, PENDING/ACCEPTED/REJECTED, trigger, session_uid, session_event_uid} linked to the session event that produced it, and accepted items can later be enabled or disabled. Hermes treats unattended reviews as fail-closed for replace and remove (staged as proposals even when approval is globally off) and offers an opt-in gate that stages every skill write with a diff, approve and reject.

items.approach: session-core agent_skills gains status (proposed, active, rejected, archived), scope (user, org), owner_user_id, origin_run_id and reason; UpsertAgentSkill for origin background_review always writes status proposed, scope user. Gateway skill matching returns only active skills in scope for the caller. New list, accept, reject and promote RPCs; promote to org requires a Control-signed admin decision (no cross-plane DB access). Frontend Settings > Learning inbox with diff, reason, source-run link and accept, reject or disable; batch weekly and auto-expire stale proposals to avoid approval fatigue; record rejections as negative examples so the same skill is not proposed again. Destructive operations from unattended reviewers are always staged. items.title: User and org memory controls: on, pause, reset and org policy
items.summary: Add a user memory state (on, paused, off) and a Reset all memory action, plus an org policy that can disable memory and the learning review, enforced in session-core at every place memory is written or read: the Dreaming loop, prefetch, save_memory, recall_memory and the skill review. Add an immediate in-chat 'remember this' path in Ask mode that confirms the save, refused under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Users and enterprise admins expect to be able to stop the assistant learning about them, and a product that learns by default needs this before it can be sold to Norwegian and EU buyers. It is table-stakes (9 of 12 sources) and today half built: you can view, correct and delete entries but not switch learning off or wipe it in one action. Raised to priority from the comparator's recommended because of the governance inconsistency described below.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude keeps topic-based entries saved during chat, each visible and editable, with 'remember' and 'forget' in chat, separate pause (keep rows, stop using and generating) and reset (erase) actions, an org opt-in on Team plans and a transcript indicator when memory is read or written. Perplexity lets the org owner switch derived features on or off for all members. Implementation shape: per-account flags generate and reference give on, paused and off; paused keeps rows but skips prefetch and extraction.

Deliver the decision to the Model Plane signed with the session or run decision (no cross-plane DB access), and enforce it in session-core in the Dreaming loop, memory_prefetch.rs, save_memory and recall_memory, and in the capability-core skill review (R-t3-08-03). Add a gateway write route for an immediate Ask-turn 'remember this' that returns a confirmation chip. Decide and document the default (the user-core default is off; the current Model Plane behaviour is on) and migrate existing users deliberately.

items.title: One policy check on every memory write path, plus guided import and safer write operations
items.summary: Add a shared deterministic memory policy in session-core (patterns for IDs, account and card numbers, credentials, plus a cheap classifier for special-category data) that runs in Dreaming, save_memory, manual create or correct, and a new ImportMemory. Add a guided import (copy a fixed export prompt, paste the answer from ChatGPT or Claude, review candidate entries, then commit) and extend save_memory to batch add, supersede and forget operations with a failure cap.
items.whyItMatters: Today the exclusion of secrets and special-category data lives only in the extractor prompt, so a model-written or hand-written memory can bypass it, which is a compliance weakness for Norwegian and EU customers. Import removes the cold start and lowers the cost of switching from ChatGPT or Claude. Superseding and forgetting let the agent correct its own memory instead of only appending.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: claude (import flow); web-claudeai (sensitive policy); hermes (write-tool mechanics)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Import: 5 of 12 (common). Sensitive-topic policy: 2 of 12 (differentiator, DOC only). Write-tool mechanics: 1 of 12 (Hermes).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude shows a fixed export prompt for the other tool, the user pastes the answer, a model call splits it into candidate entries tagged source=import that go through the normal grounding and dedup path and are shown for review before commit. Claude's documented policy is a hard never-store list plus opt-in sensitive topics with a save notice. Hermes applies a memory operations[] batch to a copy under a lock, checks the budget once on the final state, returns errors with repair hints, and ends the turn's attempts after three failures so a side effect cannot loop.

items.title: Scoped memory for Spaces, Projects and named agents with isolation
items.summary: Give agent_memory an explicit scope kind and id (user, space, project, agent), filter recall by the active scope plus allowed parents, and add a project isolation flag (nothing in from broader scopes, nothing out to them). Space memory applies only to Space turns authorised by a Control-signed Space decision and fails closed; later add an agent scope with a notes document per named agent and a Memory tab on the agents page.
items.whyItMatters: Business users mix clients and projects, and scoped memory prevents cross-project leakage while honouring the rule that Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. A per-agent memory keeps personal memory clean and fits the agents-that-work-for-you-over-time direction of the agent pages.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: web-chatgpt (project isolation contract); cursor (agent home store)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Scoped memory: 5 of 12 (common). Named persistent agents: 4 of 12 (differentiator).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: ChatGPT project-only memory defines the isolation contract: no outside memory comes in, nothing goes out, shared projects are always isolated and enterprise projects always contained; the project summary is regenerated from that project's chats only. Antigravity adds typed scopes with activation triggers and globs. Cursor gives an agent principal a small home store whose SELF.md is injected (tag-escaped) into each run and which the agent can edit, with a Memory tab listing files and source labels in Codex.

items.title: Standing user profile in the cached prompt prefix, seeded at onboarding
items.summary: Synthesise one bounded, user-editable profile memory per user on a schedule from existing memories (reusing MemoryConsolidationWorkflow), inject it as a stable block in the cached system prefix, and keep per-turn semantic recall after the cache breakpoint. Let onboarding answers write 'stated' profile memories and pass the user's timezone and locale into the platform prompt block.
items.whyItMatters: A short, stable profile is cheaper and more cache-friendly than per-turn semantic recall alone, and it makes tailoring visible in a 'what Verevon knows about you' view the user can correct. Seeding it at onboarding shortens time to personalisation for new users.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (frozen bounded snapshot; Honcho profile layer, DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: User model: 2 of 12 (differentiator). Frozen snapshot: 1 of 12. Onboarding and context defaults: 2 of 12.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes loads curated memory (about 2,200 characters) and user profile (about 1,375 characters) at session start into a cached block with a fullness meter, writes go to storage and the tool result only so the prefix cache is not invalidated, and the block is rebuilt at compaction or a new session. Honcho adds a periodic profile synthesis (session summary, user representation, peer card) refreshed every N turns. ChatGPT keeps a continually updated summary, uses time-of-day awareness and an opt-in precise location that is deleted after use.

items.title: Tone presets, a reviewed default voice and assistant-settable preferences
items.summary: Expose the existing verbosity profiles plus a handful of professional tone presets in Settings next to persona, resolved by the same instruction resolver as R-t3-08-01 so Do runs get them too. Review the platform instructions against the Hermes default-identity spec as a versioned prompt asset, and admit a narrow set of settings actions (preferences, not security or billing) to the model-executable action allowlist so the assistant can handle 'make answers shorter from now on'.
items.whyItMatters: Tone and length control is cheap, highly visible personalisation that needs no memory, and a good default voice reduces verbosity cost. Letting the assistant change a preference on request is a distinctive fit for the AI-first claim, and the governed action registry already provides the safety rails.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Personality presets: 5 of 12 (common). Default identity spec: 1 of 12. Self-configuring preferences: 1 of 12 (unique).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: ChatGPT offers seven base styles plus characteristic sliders applied immediately to all chats; each maps to a short stable system directive appended after instructions, so prompt caching is unaffected. Claude exposes a preference registry with {label, meaning, toolKey} through get and set settings tools with value lists and lock reasons, restricted to an allow-list. Hermes ships a roughly 120-word default identity covering match-length-to-ask, changed/verified/left reporting and agree-only-when-right, read only from a trusted location.

items.title: Skill authoring quality, a /learn command and skill lifecycle curation
items.summary: Phase 1: port a lessons-not-logs authoring doctrine and a memory-versus-skill routing paragraph into the sessionreview and dream_extractor prompts, and run a linter on every UpsertAgentSkill. Phase 2: add a learn command and a 'Save as skill' message action that run a Do run whose output goes through the R-t3-08-04 proposal path. Phase 3: usage telemetry and a weekly stale and archive job that never deletes, with consolidation offered as proposals.
items.whyItMatters: Learned skills are only valuable if they stay short and general; a doctrine and linter are cheap quality controls on the loop's output. /learn gives users explicit control over learning. Without retirement, learned skills accumulate and crowd the small skill-injection budget, and the same preference can land in both memory and skills.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: /learn: 3 of 12 (differentiator). Authoring quality and lifecycle: 1 of 12 (unique to Hermes).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes /learn takes a directory, URL, notes or 'what we just did' plus requirements and writes a lean index plus per-chapter references; /refine runs the review with a user focus string as an attended review. skill_manage takes operations[] (create, patch, write_file, delete) executed on copies all-or-nothing with a post-write linter (frontmatter, size caps, reference-file counts); a weekly curator marks skills stale at 14 days and archives at 30, reactivates on use, deletes nothing, limits curation to agent-created skills by created_by and keeps usage counters (load, view, patch). One routing block is shared by memory and skill reviews so each fact lands in one place.

items.title: Learn a browser procedure by demonstration inside a hosted browser session
items.summary: Record a user's workflow inside a Quarry-hosted browser session (Quarry captures the action trace and screenshots; the Model Plane only receives the trace), have a Model Plane run draft a skill from it, and send that skill through the proposal path for user review before it is saved. Desktop recording is out of scope for a web product.
items.whyItMatters: It fits the Manus-style computer-use vision: a user teaches the agent a browser procedure once instead of describing it. It is a real differentiator, but large, so it follows once core learning is proven.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Manus ships a recorder addon sharing an MCP server with computer use: it captures action events, periodic screenshots and an optional voice transcript, uploads a recording bundle, a task summarises it into steps and frames and drafts the skill file, and the user reviews it before it is delivered. Claude's Cowork has a watch-and-record mode with a teach overlay.

items.title: Self-maintained team knowledge wiki generated from activity
items.summary: A scheduled Data Plane job reads new activity through a contract with session-core (no cross-plane DB access), extracts entities and decisions, and upserts source-linked wiki pages that the Model Plane proposes and users approve, with stale marking when sources change. Space ACLs govern visibility and personal memory never enters a shared wiki without opt-in.
items.whyItMatters: Perplexity's Brain shows demand for a knowledge base that maintains itself, and Verevon already ships an org knowledge base and a Data Plane that owns wiki and graph tools. It is a strong team feature but large, overlaps the Data Plane roadmap and rests on a single documentation-only reference.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 12 sources (unique, documentation only, research preview).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An overnight refresh reads new activity, upserts markdown pages with source links into versioned storage, marks pages stale when sources change, and shows Concepts, Entities and Workstreams views; a shared project Brain has owner-controlled auto or manual updates and a personal-memory opt-in.

strengthsToKeep: Memory provenance on every answer: the memory_recall SSE event labels each memory stated, inferred or unrecorded, is saved on the turn and offers correct and forget in place; equal to ChatGPT and finer than Claude or Perplexity (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/memory_provenance.rs:103,168; sse.rs:5191; apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatMessages.tsx:2907-3243).

Feedback as a learning signal: thumbs plus reason category, server-side skill credit, an implicit-dissatisfaction classifier with Wilson-bounded quarantine and calibration rows; no reference source has all of these and Hermes has none (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/dissatisfaction.rs:1-15, implicit_feedback.rs:1-15, calibration.rs:133; apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatMessages.tsx:486-509).

Zero Data Retention propagates into learning: the RUN_COMPLETED producer withholds ZDR, waived and unknown-class runs and the review consumer fails closed unless zdr:false is declared; no reference documents anything comparable (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/learning_events.rs:172-179,288-296; apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/sessionreview/retention.go:60-80).

Temporary chat is an enforced persistence-free turn with typed refusals, not just a UI flag, which is stronger than the references' incognito modes (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/zdr_features.rs:1-12, zdr_posture.rs:146, sse.rs:8411,8513).

Dreaming extraction is at parity: a deterministic phrase matcher that already understands Norwegian ('husk at', 'jeg heter') as the floor plus an LLM extractor that treats the transcript as data, records only facts the user states about themselves, and writes with supersession, provenance and user-edit precedence (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dreaming.rs:1-8, dream_extractor.rs:128-140, memory_dedup.rs).

Two-tier memory (agent_memory plus the letta-bridge semantic tier with RRF fusion) with erasure propagated to both tiers and owner derived from the verified thread, never the caller (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/memory_grpc.rs:486-494, memory_erasure.rs).

Bounded recall pipeline: 400 ms prefetch budget, trivial-prompt gate that includes Norwegian words, outcome metrics; tighter than the Hermes design it was ported from (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/memory_prefetch.rs:90, sse.rs:5191-5256).

Server-side authored-instruction hierarchy with an explicit ADR and a context-inspector segment, ahead of most references for Ask turns (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs:6375-6440); extend it to Do runs rather than redesign it (R-t3-08-01).

Learning-loop safeguards beyond Hermes: confidence floor, protected human-authored skills and outcome-based quarantine (apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/learning/learning.go:31-39; apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/sessions.proto:851-852).

Governed typed action registry with owner plane, risk, approval metadata and forged-call denial is a stronger foundation for assistant-settable preferences than Claude's allow-list (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/action-registry.ts:2376-2398, model-eligibility.ts:127-134).
